utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before you take a decision, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw the question and I have concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Madam Fauveau, for being practical in the first place. So the time now is 1710. Mr. Haynes, just to know where you are, where you stand, we will have the break at 1755. It's 1711 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you just give me a few moments to set up?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Trivic.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yesterday you were telling us something about your role as commander of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade and the area in which it operated. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you told us that the Romanija Brigade was part of the Drina Corps. I wonder if you'd agree with me that during the period we are concerned with, namely 1992 to 1995, that the Drina Corps was defending an operational zone which included upper, middle and lower Podrinje and the Romanija plateau?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was approximately the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If you ever feel like correcting me or adding anything to that, please feel free to do so, but I'm going to try to take this fairly briefly. And it was defending those areas against the 2nd and 1st Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the 81st Division in Gorazde and the 28th Division in Srebrenica, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the main task of the Drina Corps was to defend its operational zone; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, within the operational zone of the Drina Corps, each brigade, of which you were commander of one, had its assigned combat zone; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every brigade had its own zone within the corps area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I want to ask you some questions about the zone for which you were responsible for the defence. Are you familiar with the brigade rules of the JNA of 1984?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder, therefore, in order to assist you in this task, whether we could have in e-court P408 at page 6 in the B/C/S, point 13. Sadly, although this is a partially translated document, this section is not translated, so I'm going to need your help, Mr. Trivic. Are you able to read that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Then in order that those of us who don't speak Serbian can understand it, I wonder if you would read for us point 13 so that it can be interpreted?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "For the purposes of executing a task, the brigade is given a combat area (an area of attack, area of defence, area of march and such like). Depending on the task, the brigade may be designated the territory of the combat area. The combat area is the land territory which is limited by depth and by width, wherein the brigade organises and carries out combat activities. The size of the area depends on the size of the brigade, characteristics of the features of the terrain, task, place and role in the combat disposition of several units, the situation and combat possibilities, reinforcements, strength of TO units in the area, support and such like. In the assigned combat area, the brigade commander, with all the subjects of armed combat shall organise a single system of fighting based on the objective, place and time." Should I go on reading? There is the combat territory next.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. If you could just read that and move the page across so that you can continue to the bottom of this point? And it will have to go up. Just finish the paragraph for us, please. I don't think this is so relevant.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read the combat territory, if you want me to complete the whole paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm very sorry. Could the page be put back down and across to the left, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Combat territory is free territory on the temporarily occupied territory, most often in the operational and strategic depth which is assigned to the brigade for the purposes of carrying out a task. In the combat territory the brigade commander shall, in principle, on his own initiative organise and carry out various combat activities and other activities as per the task received and in accordance with the concrete situation. The assigned territory of combat activities -- or the assigned zone of combat activities, the brigade cannot leave without the approval of the superior commanding officer. In the area of combat activities the commander shall".

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you've read enough. Now, in relation to your brigade, could you help us as to what you regarded as the area of your combat activities to be?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of combat activities of the 2nd Romanija Brigade is the territory to which the combat disposition for those particular activities is deployed. The combat disposition is the positions of the subordinate units of the brigade, that's to say battalions, where we have the forward defence line which is organised by organising the firing system and by deploying their parts of the combat establishment, logistics and so on. In addition to the battalions who take up their positions of defence, in the area of combat activity of brigade, other units are deployed, such as artillery units, with their firing positions from which they will be active, armoured and mechanised forces, command posts of battalions and brigade, logistics units and their posts, and so on and so forth. I didn't mention the anti-aircraft forces which are normally deployed to provide support to the armoured mechanised units, artillery and the brigade command post itself. This zone, together with the front defence line and the area in the rear is the designated area where all these forces are deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, I've noticed during the course of your testimony you've drawn a distinction between the phrase which has been used a lot, zone of responsibility, and the one which you've chosen, area of defence. Is it correct that during the course of the war, a phrase, "zone of responsibility" crept into certain military documents?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be said, and I in fact explained it on one occasion, that this term is synonymous with the area of combat activities and it covers an area where units are deployed. The area of responsibility or the zone of responsibility is a term that can be used, is, in fact, used only with regard to reconnaissance units as an area where they ought to obtain intelligence and information, and it is only in that context of reconnaissance units that it is termed "area of responsibility," "zone of responsibility." Now in every-day parlance, it is used as an interchangeable term for an area where unit commanders deploy their units, their forces, and where they make decisions as to their movement and engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask you now to look at another document, which is 7D441, please. Can that be placed into e-court? This document has in fact been translated, but we'll have to tie up the translation with the Serbian version later on. I want to you read, please, for us for the time being the sentence that appears after number 1, and then I'd like you to go down to paragraph C and have a look at the area of responsibility for combat operations of your brigade. If you start by just reading out for us what it says at number 1?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The areas of responsibilities for the brigades for carrying out combat activities are as follows: Brigades," and there follow the items which designate the areas more closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And would you just, please, read out for us the first couple of places that are attributed to your brigade at paragraph C?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade, exclusive of Kladanj, inclusive of Olovo, inclusive of Borovac village, exclusive of Podromanija, Kondina Glava and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's fine. So the area for which you had responsibilities for combat activities excluded Kladanj but included Olovo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But if you look above, at paragraph B, for the Bircanska Brigade, did their area of combat activity responsibility actually include Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't found it. Oh, yes, it does say in the second line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Now, I wonder if we could have into e-court, please, P02109. I think we might try blowing that up just one more time, please. And could we go up just a touch more? And to the left. No, to the right, I meant. Thank you. Now, if somebody could show you how to use the pen, which you may or may not have used in your evidence so far, I can't remember, I'm going to ask if you could mark one or two places on there for us. I'm going to ask if, as best you can, you could put Olovo on that plan for us.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Somewhere along this line, but I can't pinpoint it. I don't know what purpose it will serve for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's southwest of Kladanj, along that axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Southwest of Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you just put a dot where you think Olovo -- or an X where you think Olovo would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can I ask you a question about Olovo then? Was Olovo an area that was entirely under your control or was it an area that was substantially controlled by Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just if we could have some dates, given that compositions may have changed ethnically over the years and so forth. So if we could -- and given the length of this witness's command, it may affect the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness has heard you and he can specify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm not sure he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But do you see there is a date there the 29th of April, 1995 in the left-hand corner of this plan. I wonder if you could tell us in the spring of 1995 whether Olovo was an area that was substantially under Muslim control?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Olovo at the time was under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do you agree that the black line that is marked on that plan shows us the confrontation lines between your forces and those of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina as at the date the 29th of April of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was the line between the VRS and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do you also agree that the line we -- the line we see marked in red delineates the apparent zones of responsibility of the brigades along that front?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we take the position that those were zones for gathering intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What effective control could your brigade have over the area of Olovo?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Observing that area from the front end, that was occupied by units of the brigade, intelligence about movements, the bringing in of forces, activities, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Perhaps we can look at Kladanj. Other than intelligence, what effective control could any forces of the army of Republika Srpska have over Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And similarly, the large area of the area of responsibility of the 1st Zvornik Brigade which was behind enemy lines was effectively beyond their control or management, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move on, please? The rules that you read out referred to areas of free territory, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because we need to save it, Mr. Haynes, unless you're going to make further use of it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I would not save it just for the moment but thank you very much for your help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The rules that you read out referred to areas of free territory. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We can see within the area of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade two places noted: Nezina. Was that the place of your command?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That place is Knezina with a K. That's what I see. That was where the brigade command was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you for the pronunciation lesson. We also see there Han Pijesak. What I'd like you to mark on the map, please, for us is the location of Sokolac.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sokolac is 20 kilometres east from Knezina. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't suppose that pen is small enough for you to write Sokolac. So would you just put an S, maybe SO, under there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] This pen obviously doesn't write where I want it to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think you've done as well as any witness so far, Mr. Trivic. It can't be easy. And under the first X that you wrote, would you just put OL?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was supposed to be a lower case letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's okay. We have got what you said about it in the transcript so we'll be able to work out what it means later. Now, Han Pijesak and Sokolac were areas that were almost completely untouched by the war; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As settlements, yes. But as municipalities with their own territory, they were both affected by combat activities to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were they both municipalities that you would properly describe as coming within the free territory, as defined by the rule you read out?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And as areas of free territory, would you, as brigade commander, have had any responsibility for those areas in the absence of there being some combat activity there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only insofar as members of the brigade were concerned or affairs that were handled by municipalities for the needs of the brigade, such as supply of food and some other issues, but were part of securing properly organised life and work within the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What about responsibility for preventing or investigating crime in those areas?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crimes fall within the purview of the police, the Ministry of the Interior, the police and the judiciary. If you mean the members of the brigade were offenders?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No. Thank you. That's a perfectly fair answer. What about buildings in those areas? Could you simply seize and control buildings?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm going to seek somebody's help here. I'm told that the answer that the witness gave to the question before last was not properly translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I can assist Mr. Haynes. It is the answer of the witness recorded on page 54, line 24, "Crimes fall within the purview of the police, the Ministry of the Interior, the police and the judiciary." And this part of the answer was correctly recorded, but the rest of the answer, the witness says, "Unless we speak about brigade members." So it's basically changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you agree with that, Mr. Trivic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does that help you enough, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I shall move on. If that's the answer he gave, that's the answer he gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Could the witness please now be shown 4D478? And we are moving on to a slightly different area.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, can we save these markings?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Oh, yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, would you do us the favour of just putting your initials in the bottom left-hand corner and placing today's date on that document, which is the 22nd of May.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Can that exhibit now please be preserved?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just ask to come back to this again?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What is it you want to come back to, the plan or some other question I've asked you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map where Olovo is marked. Olovo was outside the zone. If this black line marks the zone, the existing separation line, then Olovo should be on the other side. Because I couldn't handle this pen very well, it turned out that Olovo is inside the zone on the opposite side of the separation line. So that should be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay, Mr. Trivic. You don't need to worry about it. Once we have this statement from you, that's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we are just waiting for another document to appear, Mr. Trivic, which is 7D478, and I want to ask you a question or two about that. Again, this is a document which for today's purposes, Mr. Trivic, we are going to ask you to read for us, and I wonder if you could start by reading the very top of the document so that we know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska, 30th July, 1995, obligations of units, commands and establishments of the VRS in the circumstances of the state of war that has been proclaimed in the RS. Order: Pursuant to Article 175 of the law on the army and the decision of the president of the republic proclaiming a state of war, number 011473-95 of 28th July, 1995, with a view to creating conditions for a full and more efficient execution of combat missions of army units, I hereby order: One, corps command, command of the, et cetera".

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Please stop and go down to paragraph 4 if we can be helped with that, and read that out for us.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All units on brigade level, whose area of deployment is on -- in border municipalities, are required to mark war zones along all thoroughfares, including local roads, by putting up visible hoardings, 'war zone.'"

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Again, I better check this with you. Is this a document you were familiar with as a brigade commander in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I was wounded on the 29th of July and this, as far as I can see, was written after that date, so that I didn't see this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were similar provisions in force prior to the time of your wounding?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Similar provisions appeared in some areas covered by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, although not in all theatres of war in Republika Srpska, and now allow me a minute to recall this. Since the 2nd Romanija Brigade had a peculiar role, a special role, in relation to geographical and establishment structures, in May I believe it fell within the Drina Corps organisationally. But territorially it fell within the Sarajevo Romanija region, so that I did come across one order regarding the Sarajevo Romanija region where the brigade was required to comply with that order, namely in keeping with the proclamation of war in the Sarajevo Romanija region, and to that end I took certain measures to comply with this order of the Supreme Commander in my area. I hope this was a clear answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, therefore, I think you can tell us what is the effect as a brigade commander of declaring a war zone?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, there is much more authority when the commands and authorities work together and wartime commands are established. This helped commanders in their efforts to engage troops, and we know that after three years of war, by that time there was a lot of fatigue among troops and they tried to spend as little time as possible on the lines, defending lines, preventing ambushes, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I mean, does it amount to this: That once you declare a war zone, the brigade commander has certain powers to overrule local civil authorities?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You could put it that way. I believe also military courts are established in that situation, but it affects the entire treatment of unit members and other personnel engaged in defence, to secure that they fulfil their tasks and if not, that certain measures can be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But was it the case, as with this document in your experience, that to declare a war zone, you quite literally had to mark out the area, mark the roads, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have a term here, it's not the state of war, it's a war zone. I think that's a significant difference. In border areas, it is specifically said brigades in border areas are required to mark war zones. The 2nd Romanija Brigade was not deployed in a border municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on. Can we please now have in e-court P408? This section of the document which we've seen before is translated and we need the English page 7 and the B/C/S page 15. While this document is being put on the screen for you, Mr. Trivic, it's right, isn't it, that at the time you were commander of the Romanija Brigade, you had a Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And in accordance with the rule that I'm about to show you, which is Rule 116, he was also your deputy commander; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes, in the motorised brigade, in the organisational establishment, when persons with certain responsibilities are enumerated, the Chief of Staff is at the same time deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And whilst you were away on operation Krivaja 95 and Stupcanica 95, your Chief of Staff was in command of your brigade; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder whether -- before we go any further whether the screen could be moved across to the left as we look at it so that Mr. Trivic can read Rule 116 before I ask him any more questions. Maybe I should have said "right." Can we see Rule 116, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's time for the break, Mr. Haynes. Perhaps you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We'll sort it out while we are having a break, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. 20 minutes again, please, 20 minutes break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Before I continue with this witness, I've had the opportunity of reflecting on where this cross-examination is going, and I think I should say for everybody's benefit now, it's very unlikely I will finish it this evening. I will require some of tomorrow to conclude. It may well be that the fault is mine in underestimating the amount of time my cross-examination would take, but I wouldn't be the first person to have underestimated how long they would take with this witness, and I hope people will bear with me. I apologise to everybody for any inconvenience this might cause, but there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's how it will be. At the same time I would like to you think a little bit on what's going to happen with the next one. Go ahead, Mr. Haynes, and please allow five -- would five minutes be enough for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Plenty, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please allow five minutes towards the end for Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Absolutely. Mr. Bourgon had mentioned that to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Anyway, Mr. Trivic, we were just before the break in the process of talking about the role of the Chief of Staff within the brigade and it was the Chief of Staff who acted as commander of your brigade while you were out performing operations at Srebrenica and Zepa. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you'd agree, wouldn't you, that the Chief of Staff, in accordance with his commander's order, has the power to issue orders to subordinates?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he does, in the absence of the commander, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I was moving on to that. That's a rather different situation. When the commander is absent, the Chief of Staff is in fact commander himself, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the commander is not present, the Chief of Staff is the person in command of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, some of the orders of the command are what we could call permanent orders, for example the order to defend the line is a permanent order?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is an order in accordance with the decision issued by the commander and he is in command to -- and is duty-bound to act in accordance with the decision. It is in fact his duty to carry out the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. But other orders of the Chief of Staff that do not derive from permanent orders from the commander taken by him in the absence of the commander are his commands, aren't they? They are the command of the commander?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, my objection is that there are a couple of pronouns in there. We are discussing a very technical area of command in which it is imperative that the record is absolutely clear about who we're talking about at any given time. So when we have -- when we are referring to the commander or his commands, I think we need to really specify whether we are talking about the Chief of Staff in a particular role or this individual commander, the witness himself, just so we absolutely have no question about what's being discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'll clarify it by moving on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead, then. I mean it did require some clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. It was not the greatest question I've ever asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In your absence, your Chief of Staff communicated directly with the Drina Corps as commander, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My Chief of Staff, in my absence, communicates with the command of the corps in the capacity of the most senior officer and deputy commander and acts accordingly. Evidently, you wish to clarify something that I tried to explain in my earlier statements. All the duties that derived from the decision of the commander to engage units in the area of defence, if that is what you have in mind, my Chief of Staff has to act in accordance with my decision. Should he wish to change anything, due to a newly arisen situation, he has to inform a superior command of that and then goes on to act in accordance with the feedback he received from the superior commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And by superior command, would you include corps command and Main Staff command?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above all, the corps command. He does not address the Main Staff. He does not communicate with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And I want to ask you about periods for which the commander is away. The commander might be away for a few days, say 10 days or so, or he might be away for a longer period, say a period of more than three weeks. There is little practical difference between the authority vested in the Chief of Staff, whether the commander is away for a few days or whether he's away for a period of a few weeks, is there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no significant difference, save for the fact that, like for instance when I was wounded, the issue of commanding over the brigade due to a prolonged absence, this is something that is regulated by commands governing prolonged absences. This isn't something that is regulated in the rules governing the establishment of the unit pursuant to which he is designated as the Chief of Staff and deputy commander in the absence of the commander, if I have been clear. In the case where I was absent, I was outside of the area of defence of the brigade but I was within the area of the corps, with the part of the unit that was detached and reassigned to a different area. This isn't regulated in the order on proxy. Rather, it is regulated --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last part of his answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you hear that the translators would like you to repeat the last part of your answer, please? After, "Rather, it is regulated."

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For prolonged periods of absences? Is that what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For prolonged absences, the duties are regulated pursuant to an order on standing in, or proxy, whereupon that person takes over the role of the commander until such time as a new commander is appointed formally.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I want to move on to something else, please. During the course of the war, was it commonplace for your brigade command to be visited by officers from superior command, either from the corps or from the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were such cases, and of course previously it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if a commander or a Chief of Staff came to your brigade command, they would come directly to you as commander of the brigade, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my superior were to come to the brigade command, he would first approach the brigade commander, if he's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But if we were talking about assistant commanders or chiefs of organs from the corps or the Main Staff, they would generally come to see their corresponding officers within the brigade; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Although such cases were rare. In any event, if any organ comes from a superior command, the brigade commander would be informed of this officer's coming to the command. That's a rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That may well be the case, but when officers from superior command came to the brigade, you didn't have the right or power to stop them doing their job at the brigade, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that if they announced their arrival I can stop them or prevent them from doing their job. At any rate, they would do their part of the job with the organ who is his functional corresponding post. Of course, the commander would not prevent him from doing his duty, but it is the rule that such an arrival has to be announced. Sometimes due to absence, such organs who belong to the superior structure would contact directly their -- the officer in charge of that line of job in the inferior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And if officers from superior command wished to avail themselves of your communications and other resources, you had no right to disable them by refusing them that access, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You mean yes, you could refuse them that access or no, you had no right to stop them having access to your communications and other resources?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see why I would prevent them from doing anything, if they are coming from superior command. Since we all knew each other, there were no such cases of anyone preventing anyone else from doing anything, at not in my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I believe that was the case in other brigades as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I want to move on to another topic, please, and could we have in e-court 7D480, please? Can I ask you firstly, so that we cross the appropriate hurdle, whether you were, as a commander, familiar with the instructions on sanitation or asanacija of the battlefield?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During my studies and in my career before the war broke out, these instructions were familiar to me, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I wonder whether we could go to page 4 of this document, please. I wonder, Mr. Trivic, if you could look at paragraph 4 of these instructions. Does that make sense to you? Or are there some words missing there? I think they are all there, aren't they? I wonder whether you'd agree with me that first and foremost, asanacija is an operation which is uniquely concerned with the battlefield?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I wonder whether you would further agree with me that it is not simply a question of hygiene but something rather more important than that, which we might understand if you read to us paragraph 4, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. Item 4: "The application of measures of sanitisation has not exclusively to do with hygienic and technical matters of removing the source of the infection. Rather, above all, it is a matter of general moral and humanitarian rights of people and respect for the dead and care for their families."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: For the fallen rather than the dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do you agree that that is how it was applied by your brigade and the brigades of the army of Republika Srpska during this war?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Where necessary, it had to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm going to come on to when it had to be done now, please, and if we could go to page 7 of this document. Could it go up just a little bit, please? Thank you. And I wonder whether you would be good enough to read to us paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 3: "Sanitisation is carried out immediately after the end of combat, bombing, ABH attacks and such like, as soon as the personnel designated for the conducting of a sanitisation is enabled to move freely along the battlefield, because corpses are exposed to the decomposition process outdoors, which is why their burial and cremation is made more difficult. In order for the sanitisation unit to be allowed freedom of movement before the start of their work, the battlefield ought to be cleared of mines, contaminated areas, unexploded mines, shells, aerial bombs and such like."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Could we now go down to paragraph 4 and I'd like you to read for us the second paragraph under paragraph 4, which should help determine who is responsible for asanacija.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Sanitisation in combat zones of the operations elements of the armed forces lies within the purview of the commanding officers of these particular operations, elements of the armed forces, and in addition to these, also within the purview of the authorised organs of the DPZ. Sociopolitical communities."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So it would follow from that, wouldn't it, that in the aftermath of a battle, a brigade commander would have to sanitise the battlefield both for reasons of hygiene and reasons of human dignity and have to commit significant manpower and specialist manpower to carry out that task?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the obligation of commands, to carry out that task, within their respective zones, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And is the requirement to carry out asanacija of a battlefield something which you as a brigade commander would feel it necessary to report to corps command?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of reports that are sent to superior command daily, these matters are informed about, if the unit concerned has been carrying out such activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I'm sorry to mix my terms, but I wonder whether we could now show the witness the page of this document which has the ERN numbers concluding 3980. I think it's page 5 in e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 5 or paragraph 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's page 5. Don't you worry about that, Mr. Trivic. I'd like you, if you would, to read us the very top paragraph before paragraph 5. ?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the start of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If you'd be so kind.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The feeling on the part of every soldier and officer that in the event of his wounding he will be timely provided for and in the event of his death that his remains will be taken care of with due piety and that his family will be informed in time and taken care of constitutes one of the elements of moral firmness of soldiers and officers."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you agree with the sentiment of that section of these instructions?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now can we move away from that, please? I want to ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If Mr. Haynes could deal with the source of this document, for example, whose instruction it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. This is an instruction of the army of Republika Srpska issued in 1991, and we are in the course of having the relevant passages of it translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you've looked on a number of occasions at this document, but I'm going to have put back into e-court, please, if we can, P106. You recall this document, I imagine. This is the Drina Corps preplan relating to the operation Krivaja 95 dated the 2nd of July. You've been asked to look at it by a number of my colleagues, so I'm not going to ask you to look at it in detail, but if you could just familiarise yourself, please, with paragraphs 2 A to E if that could be put up for you. You recall the document now, do you, Mr. Trivic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, the Krivaja 95 was an operation that was put together very, very quickly, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can conclude that it was. This is the order that was issued on the 2nd and as far as I remember, that command was issued on the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, if we go to the next page in paragraph 4, I might be able to help you with a few of the dates that were significant to the operation. So if we could do that, please. Let's see if we can agree this: The preorder was issued on the 2nd of July; that's right, isn't it? The forces had to be ready that day and all preparations had to be complete by the 4th of July on which date at 2.00 the IKM had to be established, and the operation had to commence on the 5th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is set out in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Also, I think that the level of reconnaissance carried out prior to the operation was the lowest level known to the army, namely commander reconnaissance. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So that we understand that, can you just explain to us what better levels of reconnaissance could be carried out in relation to any military operation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, so-called commander reconnaissance could be performed. In this case it boiled down to work on just one item, where units were given assignments and acquainted with the assessed disposition of enemy forces, whereas units that came from other areas that had not been in direct contact with enemy forces in that area, the commander thought it would be enough time to acquaint commanders of those units with it, since units were not large and it would not take up more time. That's why I think they decided to take this option. Subordinates could always, of course, use more time to find out about their axes of future engagement, to learn more about the terrain, but this was hasty organisation for performing a given task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm going to ask you to be shown one more document now, which is 7D136, which, curiously, is in English as 7D312. And I'm going to be asked if -- I'm going to ask if Mr. Trivic could see paragraph 10 of that particular document, and in particular, 10 B. Can this document go down a little bit, please, or up, or on to the next page so that he can see the whole of 10 B?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we may still require the last line on the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, if that is achievable, then that would be very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Tell me when you've read that, Mr. Trivic, would you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Given the time available for preparation of this operation, would you regard that as a very brief and probably inadequate plan for security?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The time was very short, in view of all that had to be done prior to the beginning of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you agree with the suggestion that Krivaja 95 was very much an ad hoc operation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I agree completely. It was an action that was provoked, a response to a provocation, and the corps command proceeded with a move that was defined as active combat operation and that implied short preparations and engagement of smaller forces from the corps. So this happened precisely as a result of those provocations targeting the front end of the defence line and the units that were guarding the civilian population in that area. It was a hastily organised operation because it turned out later that this part of the action, namely the separation of enclaves, could have been done in this way as well and with the engagement of larger forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I've got one last question this evening, which is: Was it difficult for you to gather these forces, and did you have sufficient time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my previous answer, I just said that subordinates could always use more time. It's a general rule. At any rate, there were other jobs, other work that had been done, although the forces were already out in keeping with the deadline that was set, 1200 hours on the 5th, parts of the rear support, reconnaissance of the terrain, and even axes for infiltration into that territory, all that was not completed within the time given, so you cannot say that the unit was prepared to act autonomously on the terrain, to be there and to perform all the tasks it was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We need to stop here for today. Mr. Trivic, you will return tomorrow in the afternoon, like today, at 2.15. Hopefully, we'll finish then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: May we move into closed session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 23rd day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 25
